SPARSE REGRESSION · GENERALIZED LINEAR MODELS

Fast variable selection.
Parsimonious models.

Fast L0 and grouped L0 regression. Accurate effects, cleaner supports, and one interface from ordinary GLMs to multinomial and survival models.

R · Dense & sparse designs · Single & multiple responses

1 millionpredictors in the high-dimensional example 39× fasterthan five-fold-CV LASSO in that example 25 / 25true rows recovered, with zero false positives

Sparse learning across a wide range of models

L0glm combines adaptive ridge with iteratively reweighted least squares, fast linear solvers and an optional relaxed refit. Small effects drop out; strong effects retain their magnitude. A shrinking active set concentrates computation where it matters, producing sparse models with excellent support recovery.

01 / MODELS

One fitting interface

Gaussian, Poisson, binomial, Gamma and inverse Gaussian GLMs; negative binomial with estimated shape; joint multinomial regression; and Cox proportional hazards.

02 / SCALE

Built for sparse signals

Dense or sparse matrices, tall or wide systems, grouped multichannel selection, and compiled SIS/ISIS screening for ultrahigh dimensions.

03 / CONTROL

Fit the model you need

Observation weights, offsets, nonnegative coefficients, unpenalized terms, normalization and original-scale estimates. Native OpenMP accelerates nonnegative identity-link Poisson fits.

04 / SELECTION

Choose your workflow

Start with a fast GIC preset, tune an information criterion, or use cross-validation with minimum-deviance and one-standard-error models. Compare methods with sparseglm().

A sparse model in a few lines 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("tomwenseleers/L0glm", subdir = "L0glm")

library(L0glm)
set.seed(7)
X <- matrix(rnorm(400 * 30), 400, 30)
y <- 2 * X[, 1] - 1.5 * X[, 8] + rnorm(400)

fit <- L0glm.fit(X, y, family = gaussian(),
  lambda = "gic", relaxed = TRUE)
summary(fit)
predict(fit, X[1:5, ])

On Windows, source installation uses Rtools. The getting-started guide covers fitting, prediction and metrics.

See the difference

Poisson spike-train deconvolution is one application: recover sharp events from a blurred, noisy signal. The same fitting machinery also handles sparse classification, overdispersed counts and survival outcomes.

Foundations

The method builds on adaptive ridge and broken adaptive ridge, with an IRLS implementation for generalized linear models. The algorithm article develops the quadratic updates and their connection to sparse penalties, drawing on Frommlet & Nuel (2016), Li et al. (2021) and Abergel, Bouaziz & Nuel (2024). It also explains screening, grouped selection and likelihood-based scoring.
